replies.author: @ahkkariq7406
replies.text:
@annabackman3028 
The term "Scandinavia" exists in various forms, the geographical definition being one of them. 
I am fully aware that there are only three Scandinavian countries, and that they share close linguistic, historical, and cultural ties. This does not preclude the existence of another interpretation of "Scandinavia"—in this case, referring to a part of Finland that offers a direct route through Sweden toward the south, should one wish to drive to the western part of the European continent. Consequently, parts of Finland are included in this context. 
This is not to say that I do not respect the Finns' desire to define themselves as being outside of Scandinavia; however, I am from Northern Norway myself, and I have frequently driven through both Finland and Sweden to reach the southern parts of Norway. The same applies to those parts of Finland that I have passed through on all those occasions.
